question_text: Conflict of interest in the public sector arises when (a) official duties, (b) public interest, and (c) personal interest are taking priority one above the other. How can this conflict in administration be resolved? Describe with an example. (150 words)
customKeyPointers: The clash is among the duty, the public interest and a personal interest
The way out is to declare the personal interest and to step out of that decision
A priority that cannot be shown in the file is the conflict

points.text: Conflict of interest occurs when personal interests interfere with official duties and public interest, compromising impartial decision-making.
Resolution mechanisms: Disclosure – mandatory declaration of assets and interests.
recusal – withdrawing from decisions where conflict exists.
code of conduct for public servants.
Example: A procurement officer whose relative owns a bidding company must recuse himself and let another officer handle the tender.
Thus, transparency, recusal rules, and institutional oversight can effectively resolve conflicts of interest.

question_text: Examine the relevance of the following in the context of civil service: (a) Transparency (b) Accountability (c) Fairness and justice (d) Courage of conviction (e) Spirit of service (150 words)
topic: Five demands on the civil service
topics: Five demands on the civil service
subTopics: Five values of the civil service
keyPointers: Transparency and the right to information
customKeyPointers: Transparency lets the act be seen
Accountability names who answers for it
Fairness, courage and a spirit of service decide what is done when nobody is watching

points.text: These values are foundational for an effective, trusted, and ethical civil service.
Transparency ensures open decision-making, reducing corruption.
Accountability holds officials responsible for outcomes.
Fairness and justice prevent discrimination and build public trust.
Courage of conviction enables standing up against pressure (e.g., whistleblowing).
Spirit of service prioritizes public welfare over personal gain.
Without these, civil services become self-serving and inefficient.
Thus, all five are indispensable for good governance and must be cultivated through training and performance appraisal.

question_text: Young people with ethical conduct are not willing to come forward to join active politics. Suggest steps to motivate them to come forward. (150 words)
customKeyPointers: A decent young person sees politics as a dirty trade and stays out
The step is a cleaner election, a visible cost for the corrupt, and a path that does not require a fortune
Motivation fails if the first experience of politics is humiliation

points.text: Ethical youth shy away from politics due to criminalization, money power, and lack of internal democracy in parties.
steps: State funding of elections to reduce dependency on black money.
lowering contest age to 21 (already done).
reservation for youth in party positions.
mandatory disclosure of candidates' criminal records.
fast-track courts for political cases.
mentorship programs by clean politicians.
and grassroots local body elections as entry points.
Also, creating a national platform for ethical youth (e.g., Youth Parliament, National Service Scheme).
Thus, structural reforms and positive incentives can encourage ethical youth to join and cleanse the political system.

question_text: One of the tests of integrity is complete refusal to be compromised. Explain with reference to a real life example. (150 words)
customKeyPointers: The test is a complete refusal, not a small compromise
A real example is an officer or a citizen who lost a post or a deal and still refused
Integrity here is the refusal itself

points.text: Integrity means consistency of actions with moral principles even under pressure; refusal to compromise is its ultimate test.
example: E. Sreedharan (Metro Man) refused a bribe of ₹5 lakh early in his career as a railway engineer. Another.

example: T.N. Seshan, as CEC, refused political pressure to dilute election monitoring, leading to landmark electoral reforms. Such individuals demonstrated that integrity is non-negotiable, even at personal cost.
Thus, absolute refusal to compromise on ethical principles defines true integrity and inspires systemic change.

question_text: Corporate social responsibility makes companies more profitable and sustainable. Analyse. (150 words)
customKeyPointers: A real duty to the community can protect a reputation and a future market
A token spend does not make a firm profitable
Sustainable means the activity can continue without using up the place it sits in

points.text: Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) is voluntary or mandated (under Companies Act 2013 for certain firms) spending on social and environmental causes.

CSR enhances profitability by building brand loyalty, attracting ethical investors, improving employee morale, and reducing regulatory risks. Sustainability benefits include resource efficiency, community goodwill, and long-term social license to operate.
Example: Tata Group's CSR initiatives have strengthened its reputation and resilience.
also be tokenistic. Genuine integration with core business strategy yields maximum benefit.
Thus, CSR, when authentic and strategic, indeed contributes to both profitability and sustainability.

question_text: "Great ambition is the passion of a great character. Those endowed with it may perform very good or very bad acts. All depends on the principles which direct them." - Napoleon Bonaparte. Stating examples mention the rulers (i) who have harmed society and country, (ii) who worked for the development of society and country. (150 words)
customKeyPointers: Ambition supplies the energy
The principle decides whether the act is a service or a harm
A great character without a limit is only a great capacity

points.text: Ambition without ethical principles leads to tyranny; ambition guided by morality leads to benevolent leadership.
Rulers who harmed society: Hitler (ambition for Aryan supremacy led to Holocaust), Idi Amin (Uganda – brutal dictatorship).

Rulers who worked for development: Ashoka (ambition to spread Dhamma after Kalinga war), Abraham Lincoln (ambition to preserve Union and end slavery). In India, Jawaharlal Nehru's ambition for scientific progress built IITs and AIIMs..
Thus, ambition is neutral; its moral valence depends on the guiding principles and whether it serves the common good.

question_text: "If a country is to be corruption free and become a nation of beautiful minds, I strongly feel there are three key societal members who can make a difference. They are the father, the mother and the teacher." -A.P.J. Abdul Kalam. Analyse. (150 words)
subTopics: Moral education at home and school
customKeyPointers: The three named are the father, the mother and the teacher
A child learns the bribe or the refusal at home and in school before the office
A beautiful mind is trained, not announced

points.text: Kalam emphasizes primary socialization agents – parents and teachers – as foundational for ethical character formation.
Parents instill values of honesty, empathy, and integrity from childhood. Teachers model and reinforce these through education. Corruption is often a learned behavior.
early moral education can prevent its normalization.
However, societal and systemic factors (poverty, weak institutions).
also matter. Kalam's point is that without moral grounding at home and school, legal and punitive.
measures alone cannot create a corruption-free society.
Thus, investing in value-based parenting and teacher training is essential for building a nation of ethically aware citizens.

question_text: How will you apply emotional intelligence in administrative practices? (150 words)
customKeyPointers: Name your own anger before it writes the order
Read the citizen's fear and do not humiliate it
The practice is a calmer hearing, not a softer law

points.text: Emotional Intelligence (EI) is the ability to perceive, understand, manage, and regulate emotions – one's own and others'.

In administration: Self-awareness helps officers recognize biases and stress triggers. Self-regulation prevents angry outbursts and hasty decisions. Empathy enables understanding citizens' grievances and staff morale. Social skills aid in negotiation, conflict resolution, and team building. For.
example, during a disaster, an emotionally intelligent officer can calm panicked victims, coordinate with distressed teams, and make balanced decisions under pressure.
Thus, EI enhances service delivery, reduces friction, and promotes a humane and effective administration.

question_text: Strength, peace and security are considered to be the pillars of international relations. Elucidate. (150 words)
customKeyPointers: Strength without peace is only a threat
Peace without security does not last
The three hold together, and a state that keeps only one of them unsettles the others

points.text: International relations rest on three interconnected pillars: strength (military and economic power), peace (absence of active conflict), and security (safety from threats).
Strength provides deterrence and bargaining power.
peace enables trade and development.
security ensures stability for diplomacy.

However, an overemphasis on strength can provoke arms races, while neglect of strength can invite aggression. Peace without security is fragile (e.g., Cold War détente). A balanced approach – cooperative security, mutual assured deterrence, and peacekeeping – underpins organizations like the UN.
Thus, these pillars are mutually reinforcing; sustainable international order requires all three to function in harmony.

question_text: The crisis of ethical values in modern times is traced to a narrow perception of the good life. Discuss. (150 words)
subTopics: A narrow idea of the good life
customKeyPointers: The good life was reduced to a private comfort and a purchase
A wider good includes the other person and the next generation
The crisis follows from that narrowing, not from a lack of rules alone

points.text: Modern society often equates the 'good life' with material wealth, consumerism, and individual success, sidelining virtues like compassion, integrity, and community.
This narrow perception fuels corruption, environmental degradation, and social alienation.
People cut ethical corners to acquire luxury goods, status symbols, and hedonic pleasure.
The crisis is evident in financial frauds (Enron, Satyam), political scandals, and rampant consumer waste.
A broader conception – eudaimonia (flourishing through virtue) or Gandhian simplicity – would reorient priorities toward relationships, service, and sustainability.
Thus, reviving a holistic understanding of the good life is essential to address the contemporary ethical crisis.

question_text: Increased national wealth did not result in equitable distribution of its benefits. It has created only some "enclaves of modernity and prosperity for a small minority at the cost of the majority." Justify. (150 words)
customKeyPointers: National wealth rose, and the rise stayed in pockets
An enclave of prosperity next to a large want is not a shared good
The ethical failure is the distribution, not the existence of the wealth

points.text: Post-liberalization, India's GDP grew rapidly, but inequality worsened. The top 10% own over 77% of wealth, while the bottom 50% hold only 13%.
Enclaves of prosperity: tech hubs (Bengaluru, Gurugram), luxury malls, gated communities for the rich.
The majority in rural areas and urban slums lack basic sanitation, healthcare, and quality education.
This concentration results from regressive taxation, crony capitalism, and inadequate social spending.
The cost to the majority includes displacement for development projects, environmental degradation, and rising living costs without commensurate wage growth.
Thus, wealth creation without redistribution and inclusive policies leads to a polarized society, contradicting the ethical principle of shared prosperity.

question_text: Discipline generally implies following the order and subordination. However, it may be counter-productive for the organisation. Discuss. (150 words)
customKeyPointers: Following an order is discipline
Following an order that is wrong, and never saying so, harms the organisation
The useful discipline includes a question, not only a salute

points.text: Discipline ensures order, predictability, and compliance with rules. But excessive or blind discipline can stifle innovation and morale.

Counter-productive aspects: Rigid hierarchy discourages subordinates from raising red flags (e.g., NASA's Challenger disaster – engineers feared breaking chain of command). Blind obedience leads to groupthink and unethical acts (Milgram experiment, Holocaust bureaucracy). Overemphasis on punctuality and formalities can waste time. Balanced discipline – 'principled disobedience' – allows constructive dissent and adaptability. Organizations.
need a culture of psychological safety where questioning is encouraged.
Thus, discipline must be tempered with ethical judgment and open communication to serve organizational goals effectively.

question_text: Without commonly shared and widely entrenched moral values and obligations, neither the law, nor democratic government, nor even the market economy will function properly. What do you understand by this statement? Explain with illustration in the contemporary times. (150 words)
customKeyPointers: A law, a government and a market all assume that people will mostly keep a promise
Without a shared moral habit, each of them needs a policeman on every act
The moral value is the ground, and the institution is what stands on it

points.text: This statement asserts that formal institutions rely on an underlying moral consensus (trust, honesty, reciprocity) to function effectively.

Without shared values: Laws become unenforceable (people evade taxes, bribe officials). Democracy fails when voters are indifferent to truth or rights (e.g., fake news swaying elections). Market economy collapses without trust (e.g., 2008 subprime crisis due to greedy lending and fraudulent ratings). Contemporary illustration: Rise of misinformation on social media erodes democratic deliberation.
corporate greenwashing undermines ethical capitalism.
Thus, moral values are the software that runs the hardware of institutions.
Therefore, legal and market reforms must be complemented by moral education and civic virtue.

question_text: You are an honest and responsible civil servant. You often observe the following: (a) There is a general perception that adhering to ethical conduct one may face difficulties to oneself and cause problems for the family, whereas unfair practices may help to reach the career goals. (b) When the number of people adopting unfair means is large, a small minority having a penchant towards ethical means makes no difference. (c) Sticking to ethical means is detrimental to the larger developmental goals. (d) While one may not involve oneself in large unethical practices, but giving and accepting small gifts makes the system more efficient. Examine the above statements with their merits and demerits. (250 words)
customKeyPointers: The honest officer sees delay, ridicule and a blocked career
The response is to keep the record, use the lawful channel, and not to match the shortcut
The difficulty is real, and it is not a reason to join it

points.text: Statement (a): Merit – realistic observation of career challenges for honest officers (victimization, transfers). Demerit – exaggerates; many honest officers rise (e.g., Armstrong Pame). Unfair practices may succeed short-term but risk long-term consequences (corruption cases).

: Merit – collective action problem, individual ethics seem futile when corruption is systemic. Demerit – one honest person can be a catalyst (e.g., Kiran Bedi reformed Tihar). Ethical minority can inspire change.

: Merit – rigid ethics might delay projects (e.g., environment clearances). Demerit – false dichotomy; sustainable development integrates ethics. Unethical shortcuts cause disasters (building collapses).

: Merit – small gifts (teeth cleaning, festival bonuses) may lubricate relations. Demerit – normalizes bribery, leads to larger corruption ('slippery slope'). Efficiency argument is flawed – gifts create obligation, not merit.

question_text: You are aspiring to become an IAS officer and you have cleared various stages and now you have been selected for the personal interview. On the day of the interview, on the way to the venue you saw an accident where a mother and child who happen to be your relatives were badly injured. They needed immediate help. What would you have done in such a situation? Justify your action. (250 words)
customKeyPointers: The interview day brings a pressure that is personal
The answer is the course that can be told later without a hidden fact
A selection bought by a compromise fails the service before it starts

points.text: Action: Stop and provide immediate first aid, call emergency services (ambulance), and arrange for their hospital admission.
If possible, ask a bystander to stay with them, or call another relative to take over.
Then proceed to the interview, explaining the delay to the board honestly.
If the injury is critical and no one else can help, I would skip the interview to save lives.
Justification: Human life and ethical responsibility to family outweigh career aspirations.
An IAS officer must prioritize public welfare even at personal cost.
The interview board would respect this decision as it demonstrates empathy, presence of mind, and moral courage – qualities essential for civil service.
Moreover, the attempt to attend the interview after ensuring help shows commitment.
If I abandon them, I would fail the very test of humanity that an officer must pass.

question_text: You are the head of the Human Resources department of an organisation. One day one of the workers died on duty. His family was demanding compensation. However, the company denied compensation because it was revealed in investigation that he was drunk at the time of the accident. The workers of the company went on to strike demanding compensation for the family of the deceased. The Chairman of the management board has asked for your recommendation. What recommendation would you provide to the management? Discuss the merits and demerits of each of the recommendations. (250 words)
customKeyPointers: A worker has died, and the family is asking for what is due
The company interest and the family's right are not the same
The head of personnel has to follow the entitlement and not hide it

points.text: Strict denial of compensation as per rules (worker's own negligence due to drinking). Merit: upholds discipline, deters future violations. Demerit: worker morale plummets, strike escalates, family suffers, negative PR.

Offer ex-gratia payment (not full compensation) – say 50% of usual amount. Merit: balances rule with compassion, may resolve strike, shows humanity. Demerit: sets precedent for leniency, may encourage false claims.
Full compensation as demanded. Merit: ends strike quickly, good will. Demerit: violates company policy, encourages irresponsible behavior, financial and legal precedent.

Mediate with workers and family: Offer full medical and funeral expenses plus a lump sum ex-gratia without admitting liability, and start a welfare fund for workers' families. Merit: pragmatic, addresses grief and strike without condoning drunkenness. Demerit: still costs money, may be seen as weak. My recommendation: Option 2 or 4 – ex-gratia with clear communication that this is one-time based on humanitarian grounds, not admission of fault. Also, implement stricter safety rules and alcohol checks to prevent recurrence.

question_text: You are the manager of a spare parts company A and you have to negotiate a deal with the manager of a large manufacturing company B. The deal is highly competitive and sealing the deal is critical for your company. The deal is being worked out over a dinner. After dinner the manager of manufacturing company B offered to drop you to the hotel in his car. On the way to the hotel he happens to hit a motorcycle injuring the motorcyclist badly. You know the manager was driving fast and thus lost control. The law enforcement officer comes to investigate the issue and you are the sole eyewitness to it. Knowing the strict laws pertaining to road accidents you are aware that your honest account of the incident would lead to the prosecution of the manager and as a consequence the deal is likely to be jeopardized, which is of immense importance to your company. What are the dilemmas you face? What will be your response to the situation? (250 words)
customKeyPointers: A hard negotiation is allowed
A bribe, a lie about the part, or a private gift to the other manager is not
Winning the deal by those means loses the firm that the deal was meant to build

points.text: Dilemmas: Duty to truth vs loyalty to company and deal.
legal obligation to give honest testimony vs potential loss of business.
harm to an innocent victim vs harm to company employees (if deal fails).

personal integrity vs career advancement. Response: I will give an honest and complete account to the law enforcement officer, including the fact that the manager was driving fast (if that is the truth). I cannot falsify or withhold crucial evidence, as that would make me complicit in a crime and violate my personal ethics. I will then inform my company of the situation and suggest alternative.
strategies to salvage the deal (e.g., negotiating with another representative of company B, or offering a revised proposal). The deal's.
importance does not justify suppressing the truth about an accident that caused serious injury. The law exists to protect life.
circumventing it for profit is morally indefensible. Moreover, lying would risk legal prosecution for perjury and destroy my reputation permanently.

question_text: A building permitted for three floors, while being extended illegally to 6 floors by a builder, collapses. As a consequence, a number of innocent labourers including women and children died. These labourers are migrants of different places. The government immediately announced cash relief to the aggrieved families and arrested the builder. Give reasons for such incidents taking place across the country. Suggest measures to prevent their occurrence. (250 words)
customKeyPointers: An illegal extra floor and a collapse that kills workers, including women
The response is rescue first, then the permission, the builder and the officer who looked away
Compassion for the families and a case against the violation have to go together

points.text: Reasons: Corruption and nexus between builders, local officials, and politicians.
poor enforcement of building codes and safety norms.
inadequate inspection mechanisms (overburdened municipalities).
use of substandard materials to cut costs.
exploitation of migrant labour (no safety training, no insurance).
weak penalties for violations (builder often gets bail).
Measures to prevent: Strict implementation of Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act (RERA) with penalties for deviations.
independent third-party structural audits at multiple stages.
mandatory geo-tagging and drone surveillance of under-construction buildings.
fast-track courts for building collapse cases.
digital building permission systems (single window) to reduce corruption.
mandatory safety training and insurance for all construction workers.
helpline for anonymous reporting of illegal construction.
stricter liability on certifying architects and engineers.
regular inspection of high-risk buildings through technology (sensors).
Also, ensure compensation and rehabilitation for victims, and create a national database of migrant workers to track their safety.

question_text: You are a Public Information Officer (PIO) in a government department. You are aware that the RTI Act, 2005 envisages transparency and accountability in administration. The act has functioned as a check on the supposedly arbitrarily administrative behaviour and actions. However, as a PIO you have observed that there are citizens who filed RTI applications not for themselves but on behalf of such stakeholders who purportedly want to have access to information to further their own interests. At the same time there are those RTI activists who routinely file RTI applications and attempt to extort money from the decision makers. This type of RTI activism has affected the functioning of the administration adversely and also possibly jeopardizes the genuineness of the applications which are essentially aimed at getting justice. What measures would you suggest to separate genuine and non-genuine applications? Give merits and demerits of your suggestions. (250 words)
keyPointers: Transparency and the right to information
customKeyPointers: The law asks for disclosure, and a pressure asks for delay or a refusal
The officer gives what the Act requires and withholds only what the Act itself protects
A personal discomfort is not an exemption

points.text: Measures to separate genuine vs non-genuine RTI applications:

Mandatory self-declaration of interest: Applicant states whether the request is for personal benefit, public interest, or commercial purpose. Merit: easy to implement, filters intent. Demerit: can be falsified, adds no real check.

Differential fee structure: Higher fees for commercial/industrial applicants; lower/nominal for citizens and non-profits. Merit: discourages frivolous filings by those with resources. Demerit: penalizes legitimate small businesses, may violate right to information principle.

Screening by First Appellate Authority: Allow PIO to refer suspicious repetitive applications to FAA for summary rejection if found vexatious. Merit: reduces harassment. Demerit: risk of misuse to suppress genuine RTIs.

Limit on number of applications per person per year (e.g., 20) unless special cause shown. Merit: curbs professional RTI activists. Demerit: arbitrary cap may hurt genuine activists exposing widespread corruption.
Digital RTI portal with unique ID tracking to identify patterns (e.g., same person filing hundreds). Merit: data-driven. Demerit: privacy concerns.

Penalty for false declarations or extortion attempts (under existing Section 18(2) of RTI Act). Merit: deterrent. Demerit: enforcement difficult. Best approach: Combination of (2) for commercial use, (3) with appeal to CIC, and (6) strict punishment for extortion. Also, strengthen CIC to deal with malafide applications promptly. Need to balance transparency with administrative efficiency.
